title: I Took the Podcast-Booth Booking to the Host Who Recorded Over Mine

parts.text: I unlocked booth B at 5:01 p.m. and host Grant was already live on my unpaid-looking leftover session. The calendar said: BOOK THE BOOTH. NINETY MINUTES. END ON THE BEEP. I was twenty-nine, guest producer, holding a calendar hold. Grant did not stop. "Hosts are the booth." I photographed the calendar, the hold, and his levels on my time. Then I logged an overlap. At 5:09 the studio manager asked why Grant's session was on my hold. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio manager can see Grant's live levels on booth B during my calendar hold.

social.video_title: He stayed live on my booked booth — Part 1/2
social.description: Podcast booth, a calendar hold, and a host still recording. I logged the overlap. Would you have knocked?

parts.text: Grant called it a take until the manager asked for the log. I printed the overlap, the photo, and the hold. He ended. Grant booked his own ninety and told producers takes were always about optics. Optics is a word hosts use when levels exist. Booking now has a second line: HOSTS END ON THE BEEP. I keep my ninety. Grant schedules. The booth finally sounds like a hold, not a leftover. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.

social.video_title: Hosts end on the beep — Part 2/2
social.description: Overlap log, ended session, and a second line. Was a take ever my hold?
